_schema.note: Data contract for a spec sheet. build.py reads one of these and renders it. Every field is either verified or absent - there is no 'estimated' state, because this document is published under LC's name to inspectors and utilities.
_schema.provenance: Each entry in `verified` names the document a number came from. A field listed in `published` but missing from `verified` is a build error, not a warning.
hard_rules: NO CONFIRMED UL/ETL LISTING = NO SHEET. Both domains. Needs ul_file_number AND ul_standard. Both examples below deliberately carry null certifications, so both BLOCK on this rule - that is the contract being documented, not a broken example.
No supplier name, model number, part-number scheme, marketing copy or branded photography anywhere.
No cost, landed cost, margin, MOQ or incoterm.
A certification appears only if verified. dlc_verified:false means the DLC line is omitted entirely.
No photometric page without a real IES file.

NEVER put a lighting field on a display sheet. No DLC line, no IES, no LM-79/LM-80/TM-21, no efficacy, no CRI, no CCT, no photometric page. A display emits content, not a distribution - see skills.json display.never_ask_for. A DLC line on a screen sheet marks us as someone who has never bought one.
_schema.categories: Two shapes, one template. `example_lighting` and `example_display` below are both rendered by overlay.py onto assets/template_LC-TP.pdf - Dino's call, 2026-09-11. The renderer is category-neutral: cover.chips takes any six label/value pairs, and `electrical` is a generic columns/rows table. Only three keys differ by category - cover.headline, electrical.title, and callout_title/callout_body.

certifications._comment: NO dlc_product_id and NO dlc_verified key on a display sheet - DLC does not apply and its presence would invite someone to fill it in. ul_standard must be NAMED (UL 48 is the likely one), not just 'UL certified'. fcc_id is the one cert here that is genuinely verifiable in a public database, so it is the one to insist on. control_system is published because Novastar / Colorlight / proprietary is a lock-in fact the customer needs - it is technical, not commercial.

example_display._no_photometrics: Deliberately absent. A display has no light distribution, so there is no IES file, no polar plot and no page 4. Do not add one.
